answer: Each identity may claim one cedar drift log stranded at the inlet after a gale, posting a 70-credit bond and a record of length and girth. An auditor recomputes its volume from the tide log, burning the bond if the volume differs by over 5 percent or the serial was already claimed. The first claim costs 31 credits; the kth costs 31 plus 6 times k minus 1, so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fakes cost 3028000 plus 70000 locked. A rented-log ring fails because each log needs a distinct funding source and a strand record. An honest salvager pays 31 once and recovers the bond after audit.
